component_records.title: Bid management, submission and RFP communications control
component_records.description: A bid manager owns the proposal as a controlled submission: the combined PDF is filed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov before the RFP's stated proposal deadline, with the submission treated as time-of-the-essence and a receipt notification from MoDOT obtained as proof of submission. The same workstream files any questions or comments to the same address before the question deadline in Section 1E, and enforces the RFP's rule that e-mail to that address is the only permitted contact with MoDOT — no employee is approached by any other route. All RFP events the team attends or triggers (question window, proposal filing, interviews, kick-off and milestone meetings) are scheduled inside the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window, and the bid calendar is built with Central-time cutoffs and internal buffers so no deadline is missed by a time-zone or send-versus-receipt error.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement against a finalized work plan that details every task, the resources assigned and the schedule, and that is submitted for MoDOT's approval — the plan explicitly records MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans and any changes to them. The component delivers the kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review work plan, scope and schedule and to set the protocol for ongoing communication; quarterly status meetings (in person or online) reviewing the prior period and the next; written minutes for the kick-off and every quarterly meeting; and a standing e-mail/phone channel to MoDOT contacts for continuous progress updates. It also carries the consultation duty with MHTC's representative on any administration concern, and full coordination with the Construction and Materials Division, including making advice and information available throughout the agreement. Quarterly progress content is packaged so the Division can feed it into the SPR Quarterly Report.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance lead owns every non-technical obligation in one place: acceptance of the post-award negotiated contract and its provisions, including MHTC's right to cancel the award if terms cannot be agreed; no public release of material without MHTC's prior consent; no assignment or delegation without written consent; formal signed amendments for any change; and full responsibility for subcontractor performance. The component delivers the E-Verify MOU documentation, the sworn affidavit of non-employment of unauthorized aliens, Executive Order 07-13 compliance, and flow-down of the required subcontract provisions with enforcement action as the Commission directs. It also stands up records management (working papers retained and available to MHTC and the State Auditor at no charge during the term and three years after final payment), confidentiality handling with immediate notification of any third-party request, and certificates of general liability ($500,000 per person / $3,000,000 per occurrence), automobile liability at the same limits, and Missouri workers' compensation. All deliverables and MHTC-supplied information are assigned to MHTC, with no royalty or fee on derived products.

component_records.title: Pricing, cost estimate and fee proposal
component_records.description: A cost estimate built on the RFP's own line structure — Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A), Miscellaneous, and Total — priced as a whole-of-contract total within the $175,000 not-to-exceed cap, with miscellaneous costs itemized on an additional sheet. The fee proposal is presented on the PRICE PAGE and the MoDOT cost estimate template, and the bid commits to performing at the quoted fees under the RFP's terms. Effort is allocated across the four phases so the price is traceable to the work plan, and the estimate is built to survive the post-award negotiation without scope or price movement.

component_records.title: Kick-off, Data Management Plan and program approval gate
component_records.description: The first two weeks after kick-off deliver the Data Management Plan, describing the anticipated formats of all project data and files and committing to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the data stays usable to MoDOT after the study. In parallel the team names the program it will use to develop LLDs and submits it — with version, licensing, hosting model and security documentation — for MoDOT Information Systems approval, and holds Task 3c (proof of concept) until that approval is in hand. This component is the schedule's critical gate: nothing downstream starts until the DMP is accepted and the program is approved.

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML right-of-way practice
component_records.description: A structured search and review of how other state DOTs use AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, DOT reports and peer-state practice, delivered as a written review with an annotated source list and a synthesis of what is transferable to MoDOT's metes-and-bounds drafting workflow. The review is scoped with MoDOT at kick-off (states, period, publication types, ROW use cases) so 'thorough' has an agreed definition, and its findings feed both the proof-of-concept design and the final report.

component_records.title: LLD drafting engine configured to MHTC parameters and EPG 236.4.6.2
component_records.description: The core technical build: an AI/ML drafting capability that takes parcel and right-of-way inputs and produces a first-draft legal land description for MoDOT Right of Way staff to review and edit. Drafting rules are encoded from MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 and the MHTC parameters agreed at kick-off: metes and bounds for partial takings, verbatim last-deed-of-record language where a property is acquired in its entirety, and explicit recitation of the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased whenever title is less than fee simple. Output is a structured draft with the source inputs and rule references attached, so a reviewer can see why each call was made, and the engine is built to be corrected — reviewer edits are captured as feedback for the next iteration.

component_records.title: Proof of concept and MoDOT demonstration
component_records.description: A working proof of concept that generates draft legal land descriptions across a variety of property types, run on real MoDOT cases and demonstrated to MoDOT staff at the 4/25/2025 presentation, with sample outputs and a walkthrough of how each draft was produced. MoDOT reviews the drafts and returns improvement feedback; the team runs a defined number of revision cycles and re-demonstrates, with the interim presentation by 9/15/2025 reporting measured results — accuracy against surveyor-reviewed descriptions, reviewer edit effort, and where the tool should and should not be trusted. The proof of concept is the evidence base for the final report's findings.

component_records.title: Hosted web application on MoDOT-approved technology stack
component_records.description: The finalized system is delivered as a browser-based web application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, built on the RFP's approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ only where specifically needed), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, in C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML, with Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use. It meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard, runs on Oracle 19C for on-premise deployment, stores no PII without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval, and uses no third-party tool that would put a licensing obligation on MoDOT without prior BRPT and IS management approval. Library dependencies are reviewed annually, and no third-party copyrighted content or vendor branding is embedded where a licensed option exists to remove it.

component_records.title: ROW staff training and user manual
component_records.description: Once the system is finalized, the team trains MoDOT Right of Way staff on it and hands over a user manual written for reviewers rather than developers: how to load a parcel, read a generated draft, apply the EPG 236.4.6.2 checks, edit and approve, and record feedback. Training is delivered in sessions sized with MoDOT at kick-off, in person or online, with the manual as the reference document and the training materials left with MoDOT. The manual is delivered in draft with the 11/3/2025 draft deliverable set and finalized with the final report, so staff are trained on the same version that is handed over.

component_records.title: Reporting, research summary and close-out
component_records.description: The close-out package: a final report detailing every task completed and all findings generated during the project, including the literature review, proof-of-concept results and measured performance; a 1–2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions; and a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing the significant details of the project. Draft report, summary and user manual are submitted on 11/3/2025 for MoDOT review, revisions are incorporated, and the final set is delivered before the final invoice on 2/2/2026. All documents follow the RFP's publication guidelines and are delivered in the formats MoDOT specifies, with ownership assigned to MHTC.

items.text: LLD drafting rules (EPG 236.4.6.2) and MHTC parameters are not in the RFP. It is also unclear whether the AI output itself must satisfy the standard or only the surveyor-reviewed final description. The rule set is the heart of the technical build and is referenced but absent; the RFP also leaves open whether the AI draft or only the human-reviewed output must comply, so a wrong reading is likely unless MoDOT supplies the text and confirms the standard.

items.text: MoDOT Information Systems approval of the LLD program gates the whole schedule. The proof of concept cannot start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named LLD development program, and the RFP does not say what documentation must accompany the name or what criteria and timeline the approval uses. If approval is slow or the chosen program is rejected, the 4/25/2025 demonstration and every later milestone slip while the fixed contract end date of 2/2/2026 does not move. The proposed solution assumes approval within four weeks, which is an assumption, not a commitment from MoDOT. A hard approval gate sits on the critical path before the first technical deliverable, and the RFP settles neither the submission package nor the approval duration; the four-week assumption is the bidder's own.
items.reason: Approval gate, 4/25/2025 demo and 2/2/2026 end are supported; the four-week assumption and 'whole schedule' gating are not in the sources.

items.text: Fixed milestone dates conflict with a 15-month contract period. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes a 2/2/2026 contract end and final invoice, which from the estimated November 2024 start is roughly 14.5 months, and the milestone table says dates will be determined at kick-off. If the start slips past November 2024, the fixed end date compresses the work and the final report, summary, presentation and training must be delivered in less time at the same not-to-exceed price. The two duration statements cannot both hold, and the RFP itself says the schedule is an estimate to be finalized in contracting, so a compressed or shifted schedule is plausible.
items.reason: 15-month period and 2/2/2026 end are supported, but 'estimated November 2024 start', 'schedule is an estimate' and 'roughly 14.5 months' are not stated; kick-off 11/15/2024 is.

items.text: Fixed $175,000 cap against an open-ended research scope. The services are capped at a not-to-exceed $175,000, while the RFP defines scope partly by reference to task descriptions it says are only guidance and leaves the literature review, proof-of-concept volume, training and 'accompanying documentation' open-ended. If MoDOT reads the scope broadly, the fixed price covers more work than was costed, and the bidder absorbs the overrun. A hard cap combined with several undefined scope drivers means the price can be consumed by work the bidder did not size; the impact is a budget overrun on a fixed-price contract.
items.reason: Not-to-exceed $175,000 and guidance-only task descriptions are supported; 'fixed-price contract' is not stated, and the open-ended scope claims are partly interpretive.

items.text: Python and third-party tooling may need IS approval the schedule does not allow. The proposed solution builds the drafting engine on the RFP's approved stack with Python confined to small uses, but an AI/ML drafting capability will plausibly need Python libraries or a third-party model or service, and both large-scale Python use and any tool placing a licensing obligation on MoDOT require prior BRPT and IS management approval. If approval is refused or slow, the technical approach must be redesigned late, and the RFP does not define what counts as large-scale Python use or how long approval takes. The approved-technology rules are strict and the AI/ML work naturally pulls against them, while the approval thresholds and timelines are unstated; a redesign after the proof of concept would hit the fixed milestones.
items.reason: Facts on Python limits, BRPT/IS approval and unstated thresholds match sources; the rest is judgment and bidder approach.

items.text: Draft deliverable date conflicts with the two-months-prior rule and the user manual. The RFP fixes 11/3/2025 for the draft final report, summary and user manual, but also says draft documents are due about two months before the final report, and separately requires the user manual as part of training. The proposed solution delivers the manual in draft on 11/3/2025 and finalizes it with the final report, which may be later than MoDOT expects and may leave staff trained on a document that is still changing. Two dates for the same deliverable set are stated and the training/manual sequencing is not settled, so a mismatch with MoDOT's review cycle is plausible; the impact is rework and a compressed review, not project failure.
items.reason: 11/3/2025 draft date, two-months-prior rule, and manual in training are all in sources; the remainder is judgment.

The proposed solution assumes a small number of sessions for the ROW review team with the manual as the only material beyond slides; if MoDOT expects statewide training or a print-ready manual, the effort grows well beyond the priced scope inside a fixed $175,000 cap. The scope drivers that set training cost are all unstated, and the solution's assumption is the bidder's own; the impact is material rework or unpaid effort rather than failure.
